surprises.description: The Board authorized an incremental $5 billion buyback, bringing total authorization to about $6.3 billion, and management said it would accelerate repurchases in Q4 and 2027. The preview highlighted that Q2 buybacks had been light at $104 million, but did not anticipate a program of this size.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Board authorized an incremental $5 billion share repurchase program, bringing total authorization to about $6.3 billion”; management is “committing to accelerate buybacks in Q4 and 2027.”

surprises.description: NXP now expects 2026 pricing to be neutral rather than declining by low single digits, and said historical annual price erosion should moderate structurally. That is a better pricing outlook than the prior forecast, with an additional longer-term improvement not flagged in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Pricing is now expected to be neutral for 2026 (versus an initial low-single-digit decline forecast),” and management expects “the historical pattern of annual price erosion to structurally moderate.”

surprises.description: NXP raised its data-center outlook beyond the prior $500 million forecast for this year and now expects the business to exceed $1 billion by 2028. The preview sought first-time data-center sizing, but did not anticipate this higher outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Data center revenue is now expected to exceed the prior $500 million outlook this year and surpass $1 billion within a couple of years (by 2028).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Any first-time sizing of data-center or physical-AI revenue directly rebuts the downgrade.”

surprises.description: Q4 gross-margin guidance is 59%, above the preview’s 58.5% consensus and base-case expectation of 58.5–58.7%. Management also described margins rising above 60% in 2028, beyond the preview’s focus on reaching 60% during 2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: Q4 guidance calls for “gross margin of 59%”; management expects gross margin to reach “60% during the year” in 2027 and be “above 60% in 2028 with VSMC ramp.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Guide mid is 58.5%”; the base case expected “GM 58.5–58.7%,” and the preview focused on the “60% 2027 target.”

surprises.description: The preview anticipated longer lead times in parts of the portfolio and rising escalations, but the call described much broader tightness: 80% of lead times now exceed 16 weeks, versus 25% a year ago. Book-to-bill was well above 1 across all end markets and regions, and backlog extends into 2027, supporting demand strength while leaving supply constraints as a risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Book-to-bill remained well above 1 across all end markets and regions,” backlog “continues to grow and extend into 2027,” and “80% of lead times now exceed 16 weeks versus only 25% a year ago, with customer escalations up sizably.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Lead times >16 weeks in parts of the portfolio and customer escalations doubled q/q in Q2”; the preview said rising lead times with flat inventory could indicate “genuine tightness,” but could also “cap upside to the quarter.”

surprises.description: NXP disclosed that SDV revenue is already running above $1.5 billion annualized and remains on track for a $2 billion 2027 target. The preview asked for SDV/VW ramp economics and timing but did not give an expectation for revenue at this scale.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SDV revenue running above $1.5 billion annualized and on track for the $2 billion 2027 target.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked about “VW Group named S32K5 the zonal-controller MCU” and said “Dollar content, timing, and whether this is incremental to the existing pipeline are the questions.”

surprises.description: Industrial revenue grew nearly 50%, ahead of the preview’s roughly 40% industrial growth read-across. The call also quantified AI-enabled processors at about 15% of industrial/IoT processor revenue in 2026, more than doubling from last year.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The industrial portion growing nearly 50%” and AI-enabled processors are “expected to reach ~15% of industrial/IoT processor revenue in 2026, more than doubling from last year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “industrial +40% y/y” as a supportive read-across and noted a “$1.5B design-win pipeline across 200+ customers.”

surprises.description: NXP raised CapEx to about 5% of revenue to add back-end capacity and build a Malaysia facility ready for 2028. The preview discussed JV investment but did not flag this increase in NXP’s own capacity spending.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Raising CapEx to about 5% of revenue to add back-end capacity and build a Malaysia facility ready for 2028.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s secondary watch list mentioned “VSMC/ESMC JV capex (~$2.4B committed, 70% of plan),” but did not state an expectation for NXP’s own CapEx.
